# The console's permissions map

Every capability the console knows, who holds it by default, and every API route that needs it. This page is generated from the code and never edited by hand. After a change to a route, a capability, a role default or a page, regenerate it with:

```sh
npm run permissions:map
```

`test/route-permissions.test.ts` fails when this file differs from what the code says, so it cannot drift. Route paths are relative to `/dashboard/backup/app/api/`.

## How access is decided

1. Every API route declares one capability. The router checks it before the route's handler runs and, when the person lacks it, answers 403 with a message in plain words ("You cannot start a backup. Ask the Owner if you need access.") and the capability id in a separate `need` field.
2. A capability that is not in the catalog is refused, and so is every system actor: capabilities belong to people.
3. A personal deny beats every allow, and a personal allow stops working at its end date. A power given for a while (at most 90 days, asked for and approved in cf-admin) counts until its own end, even after the grant's end date; a deny still beats it, and a floor can never be one.
4. A floor can be held only by Vendor support and Owner. No policy and no personal grant can give it to anyone else.
5. The defaults on this page are the code's. The Access page can change what a role holds and give or take away capabilities for one person, so what someone holds today can differ from what is listed here. The Access page shows the result.
6. Every route that changes something carries an audit action. A read carries none in the route table, except that the reads which hand over a file's content stamp their own line from the handler, and cf-admin records it (named in "Also checked in the handler").
7. A few handlers check one more thing beyond the capability the router enforced, such as a sign-in within the last 10 minutes. They are named in "Also checked in the handler" and are proved by tests.
8. A grant saved through cf-admin's Access Center belongs to the cf-admin account it was saved for. Someone signed in under another account with the same email gets nothing from it and starts from their role. A grant saved before accounts were recorded follows the email.
9. The router reads the access policy from a copy each isolate keeps for 30 seconds. A route whose capability is destructive, secret or admin reads the stored policy instead, so taking one of those away stops it at once. Saving a person's access and downloading backup data in Files also decide on the stored policy.
10. Before any of this, cf-admin's gateway has checked that the person may open the Backups page, and it refuses every change from a Viewer. This Worker answers only a request that carries cf-admin's actor header and, once `CONSOLE_SIGNING_KEY` is set, cf-admin's signature over it (RULES.md rule 2).

## Roles

From the most senior role down. These are the code's defaults.

| Role | Holds by default |
|---|---|
| Vendor support | Every capability (32) |
| Owner | Every capability (32) |
| Admin | 12 of 32: `console.view`, `runs.view`, `logs.view`, `usage.view`, `activity.view`, `config.view`, `runs.annotate`, `logs.download`, `activity.export`, `access.delegate`, `files.view`, `restoretests.view` |
| Manager | None |
| Staff | None |
| Viewer | None |

cf-admin refuses every change from a Viewer before it reaches this Worker, so only a read capability given to a Viewer takes effect.

## Capabilities

Grouped by class: read, operate, destructive, secret, admin.

### `console.view`

Open the console; see status and what is running now.

- Class: Read.
- Held by default by: Vendor support, Owner, Admin.
- Floor: no.
- Needed by: `GET health`, `GET live`, `GET access/catalog`, `GET access/person`, `POST access/person`.
- Opens: Overview, Live.

### `runs.view`

Run history and run detail.

- Class: Read.
- Held by default by: Vendor support, Owner, Admin.
- Floor: no.
- Needed by: `GET runs`, `GET runs/:runKey`, `GET runs/:runKey/report`.
- Also checked in the handler of: `GET live`.
- Opens: Runs.

### `logs.view`

Logs, the live log, live metrics, GitHub archive viewer.

- Class: Read.
- Held by default by: Vendor support, Owner, Admin.
- Floor: no.
- Needed by: `GET live/:runKey/log`, `GET runs/:runKey/report/log`.
- Also checked in the handler of: `GET live`.
- Opens: no page.

### `usage.view`

Usage, allowances, the viability view.

- Class: Read.
- Held by default by: Vendor support, Owner, Admin.
- Floor: no.
- Needed by: `GET usage`, `GET readiness`, `GET diagnostics`.
- Opens: Usage, Health.

### `activity.view`

Who did what, when.

- Class: Read.
- Held by default by: Vendor support, Owner, Admin.
- Floor: no.
- Needed by: `GET activity`, `GET alerts`, `GET digest`.
- Opens: Alerts, Activity.

### `config.view`

## Console pages

A page opens for a person who holds its capability (src/ui/page-caps.ts); a person without it is sent to Overview. Whatever a page reads or changes, the server still checks the capability of each request it makes.

| Page | Opens with |
|---|---|
| Overview | `console.view` |
| Live | `console.view` |
| Runs | `runs.view` |
| Files | `files.view` |
| Usage | `usage.view` |
| Health | `usage.view` |
| Restore tests | `restoretests.view` |
| Access | `access.view` |
| Keys | `keys.status` |
| Alerts | `activity.view` |
| Activity | `activity.view` |
| Settings | `config.view` |

## How the console shows it

A control the person may not use stays visible and disabled, with its reason in the same plain words as the refusal ("You cannot start a backup. Ask the Owner if you need access."). It is hidden only where showing it would reveal something the person may not know. The rules are in section 5 of the console's design system, `docs/reference/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` (private to this repository).
